# v1.8.1 — Hotfix: macOS startup crash + `{platform}` template KeyError

A focused hotfix for the two critical bugs that surfaced within an hour of v1.8.0 publishing. Anyone on v1.6.0, v1.7.0 or v1.8.0 (all of which were flipped to Pre-release) should upgrade to this build.

## What's fixed

- **MeedyaDL no longer crashes on first launch on macOS (#827).** The new external queue watchdog from v1.8.0 was calling `tokio::spawn` from the Tauri setup closure, which on macOS runs on the AppKit main thread before the Tokio runtime is registered as current. The call panicked across the `extern "C"` FFI boundary tao uses for AppKit and aborted the process before the UI loaded. The watchdog now uses `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`, which looks up Tauri's runtime handle directly and is safe to call from any thread. Linux and Windows builds were unaffected.
- **Downloads no longer fail with `Error processing "...": 'platform'` (#829).** The `{platform}` template variable was added to the frontend registry in v1.0.x (#309) for multi-service preparedness, and v1.6.0's #800 added the `[Platform]` chip to every Folder Template and File Template builder by default. **The corresponding backend substitution was never implemented**, so MeedyaDL wrote `{platform}` verbatim into GAMDL's `config.ini` and GAMDL's Python `str.format(**metadata)` raised `KeyError: 'platform'` on every download. MeedyaDL now substitutes `{platform}` → `"AppleMusic"` in both the `config.ini` write path and the CLI-arg path before handing the template off to GAMDL. Users who were affected can put the chip back into their templates — it now produces `AppleMusic/Artist/Album/...` as intended.

## Notes

- **v1.6.0 / v1.7.0 / v1.8.0 are still flagged as Pre-release** on the GitHub Releases page with a Known Issues banner. The auto-updater will offer v1.8.1 to anyone on those builds. After you've installed v1.8.1, the previous Pre-release banner stops being relevant — both bugs are fixed here.
- **4 new unit tests** in `config_service::tests` cover the `{platform}` substitution (happy path, multi-occurrence, short-circuit when absent, end-to-end INI write). All 1,184 existing tests still pass.
- **Defensive convention noted in code:** `queue_watchdog::spawn_queue_watchdog` now carries a doc-comment block explaining the `tokio::spawn` vs `tauri::async_runtime::spawn` distinction at setup-closure call sites, so future setup-time helpers don't make the same mistake.
